The T0 timing pilot ran the real d5s7 teacher on 2 probe seeds: game 1 finished 75 moves in 2,479 s under concurrent smoke-test load (~33 s/decision); single-root d5s7 timing on a quiet machine measured 9.5-13.6 s on live early/mid boards and ~0.01 s near-terminal, with transposition-table size (1M/4M/16M) making no material difference. Teacher game lengths are heavy-tailed: the second pilot game (seed 0xa5277501) was still running after 2 hours and was then stopped, its diagnostic point made — a small share of teacher games can run for hours at the 2,000-move cap, so the corpus stage must use a per-game move cap (e.g. --move-cap 500, a disclosed operational parameter the frozen protocol leaves open) as well as the resumable per-game part-file writer and a wall sub-budget. Consequence recorded in the experiment plan: the corpus stage costs ~10-14 CPU-s per root; 512 games project to roughly 10-16 wall-hours on 16 dedicated cores, inside the frozen 24 h budget with the partial-corpus stop as the safety valve.
